In summary, our research is concerned with
a theoretical study of the semileptonic decay modes of $\Lambda_b$.
the study of the semileptonic decay $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda c \ell \bar \nu_{\ell}$, where $\ell=e,\mu,\tau$, in the heavy-quark limit.
the study of the Isgur–Wise function in the framework of the diquark model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the diquark picture of baryon structure is not only a useful tool for the study of baryonic properties, but also a powerful theoretical approach in the study of b-baryon decays.
the Isgur-Wiese function is a very useful tool to understand and interpret heavy quark spectroscopy.
the diquark model is able to reproduce the main features of the experimental results for the $\Lambda_b$ decays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the infrared regime for heavy-quark is essential for description of the observables of the semileptonic $\Lambda_b$ decay.
the diquark model gives a good qualitative description of the semileptonic $\Lambda_b$ decays.
the diquark model is in good agreement with experimental data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diquark model can be used for description of the heavy baryon decays in the infrared regime.
the Isgur-Wide function for the $\Lambda_b$-baryon is not suppressed in the whole kinematically allowed range.
